Local Procrustes Error

Source: R/local-procrustes.R
local_procrustes.Rd

Measure how closely each reference neighborhood retains its geometry in an embedding after allowing translation, rotation, and reflection. Each patch contains its anchor and the same k reference neighbors in both spaces.

Usage

local_procrustes(
  Xin,
  Xout,
  k = 15,
  nn_method_in = c("brute", "nnd"),
  is_transposed = FALSE,
  n_threads = 0,
  nn_in = NULL,
  ret_extra = FALSE
)

Arguments

Xin

Reference coordinates, as a dense numeric matrix or data frame.

Xout

Embedding coordinates for the same observations in the same order. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored in both inputs.

k

Number of reference neighbors per anchor. The anchor is included in addition to these neighbors.

nn_method_in

Reference neighbor search method. Use "brute" for exact search or "nnd" for approximate neighbor descent.

is_transposed

Whether observations are stored in columns rather than rows.

n_threads

Maximum number of threads to use. 0 or 1 runs serially.

nn_in

Optional reference neighbor graph, such as nn_in from a detailed nn_preservation() result. Its first k non-self indices are used in each row. Supplying it skips neighbor search.

ret_extra

Whether to also return the row-aligned residuals and graph.

Value

The mean residual over defined reference patches, or NA_real_ when all are undefined. With ret_extra = TRUE, a list with error, pointwise_error, n_defined, and nn_in. The pointwise vector follows the rows and names of the reference observations.

Details

Coordinates are centered within each patch. The alignment uses orthogonal least squares, with zero padding to compare different dimensions. Scale is fixed. To account for arbitrary embedding units, multiply the entire embedding by a single calibration factor before calling this function.

The residual is the sum of squared aligned coordinate differences divided by the reference patch's centered sum of squares. Zero indicates exact agreement up to numerical precision. Values can exceed one. A constant reference patch has an undefined residual (NA_real_). Moving an intact group can leave its internal patch scores unchanged.

Automatic neighbor search uses Euclidean ordering. Supplied graphs select the patch members in their given order. The Procrustes fit always uses the coordinate geometry of Xin and Xout.

Scaling

Each alignment uses one patch of k + 1 observations. With k fixed, the number of fits grows linearly with N. The default brute-force reference search compares all pairs. Supply nn_in to reuse a reference graph across embeddings, or use nn_method_in = "nnd" to find approximate neighbors.

References

Goldberg, Y., & Ritov, Y. (2009). Local Procrustes for Manifold Embedding: A Measure of Embedding Quality and Embedding Algorithms. https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2669 Quadra follows their construction by matching the same observations in both patches. The fit keeps scale fixed within each patch. ZADU 0.5.4 selects neighbors separately in each space.

See also

nn_preservation(), local_radius_correlation()

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
embedding <- prcomp(x, rank. = 2)$x
result <- local_procrustes(x, embedding, k = 10, ret_extra = TRUE)
result$error
#> [1] 0.304925
head(result$pointwise_error)
#> [1] 0.4039810 0.2655268 0.4390545 0.2287525 0.3931438 0.2965453
